result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep all five colors, say plainly that the palette works, and add no new accent hues or gold. A is tighter and more decisive: its three small additions are tied to concrete problems (tag contrast, hover state, card surface). B adds more extras (second paper tone, hairline color, deeper rust) and wanders into typography, photography and print advice, so it reads closer to a mini redesign, even though its point about where premium feel comes from is useful. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep the five colours and stick to one accent. B gives a clearer reason for keeping the palette (one accent, warm paper, tinted ink instead of black), and its contrast figures are more accurate: Ink on Paper is about 13:1, and B correctly works out Ink on Sage at about 4.3:1. A frames four additions as things the palette needs and says a single flat background looks less finished, which leans toward inventing problems. A's advice on photography and typography is a good pointer to where premium feel comes from beyond colour.
